name: alice and an ice-lite server

input.local:
a=candidate:1 1 udp 2130706431 192.168.1.42 50004 typ host
a=candidate:2 1 udp 1694498815 192.0.2.10 54321 typ srflx raddr 192.168.1.42 rport 50004
a=candidate:3 1 udp 16777215 198.51.100.50 49152 typ relay raddr 192.0.2.10 rport 54321

why: The post's call: three local candidates against the server's one host. The srflx pair is pruned, since its base is the host address and it would send the host pair's check; two checks run, host first.

fields.label: In short
fields.value: 2 checks run, starting with host to host. 1 pair is dropped because it would send the same packet from the same place as a better pair. 1 check goes through a relay, so it comes last.

fields.label: Controlling
fields.note: its candidate priorities are G in the formula; the other side's are D

input.remote:
a=candidate:1 1 udp 2130706431 10.0.0.8 61000 typ host
a=candidate:2 1 udp 1694498815 198.51.100.77 40100 typ srflx raddr 10.0.0.8 rport 61000
a=candidate:3 1 udp 16777215 198.51.100.51 49200 typ relay raddr 198.51.100.77 rport 40100

why: Both sides full agents with host, srflx and relay: nine pairs. The three that use the local srflx candidate are replaced by its base, the host address, and pruned; the remote srflx stays, since only local candidates are replaced. Six checks.

a=candidate:1 1 udp 2122260223 7f3c1b2e-4d5a-4b6c-8d7e-9f0a1b2c3d4e.local 50004 typ host
a=candidate:2 1 udp 2122262783 2001:db8::42 50006 typ host
a=candidate:3 1 udp 1686052607 192.0.2.10 54321 typ srflx raddr 0.0.0.0 rport 0

why: A browser's mDNS name pairs with the IPv4 server; the IPv6 host does not, and the srflx with a hidden raddr cannot be traced to its base, so it is kept.
